title: The watering shot plays in a corner while she keeps control
tier_reason: It is the first Lab loop a new player sees in play, and Q-104 ruled it must never take control away.
ask: Build Q-104's ruling as written in design/13 'The watering shot' and design/09 The inset. The first time the neighbour waters during the cold open (her 'water' action through apply_action with actor 'neighbour'; systems/sim/cold_open.gd derives it), an inset card fades up in a corner of the screen showing the watering_beam loop from assets/anim/watering_beam/ (export item) at ×1, nearest-neighbour, on the Lab's sky colour, plays one pass at the manifest's rate, and fades down. It takes no input, sits in a corner the HUD's corner map leaves free (the HUD's interactive controls are corner cards; the inset must not cover one, nor the neighbour, nor the player), and plays once per farm. Presentation only: it is driven by watching the recorded action, never by anything the sim does differently. Headless runs skip it. Capture a PNG with a display and attach it.
first_action: Read ui/hud.gd's corner assignments and world/farm.gd's action-report path the crow's animation already listens to, and hang the inset off the same signal.
source_message: Filed from the 2026-09-10 brainstorm on where the Animation Lab loops enter play (P-15, Q-103, Q-104).
result:
I built Q-104: the first time the neighbour waters in the cold open, a card fades up in the screen's top-left corner — the loop of water hitting the wheat's soil, at native size, on its own dark canvas — plays through once, and fades out. She keeps walking, the player keeps full control, nothing about the farm itself changes.

**Where it hooks in.** Every action that resolves already passes through one spot in `world/farm.gd` (`_record`) — the same spot that already gives a non-player actor's verb its sound and puff. I added one more check there: the first time it sees `water` from the neighbour, it tells `main.gd`, which tells the HUD to play the loop. It's watching the recorded action, exactly as asked — nothing in the sim or the cold-open script knows this exists.

**Where it sits.** I read the HUD's actual layout rather than guessing: the bed button owns bottom-left, the held-item card bottom-right, the menu button top-right — top-left holds only the day/weather readout inside the thin top strip, so the space below it is genuinely unclaimed. I captured a real frame from the running game to check it (`tools/shot_watering_inset.png`, viewable above) — the card sits clear of every HUD control, and clear of both her and the neighbour in that shot.

**One thing worth knowing.** "Once per farm" is tracked as a flag in memory, not saved — deliberately, since the alternative would mean the presentation touching the save format, which is exactly what this was ruled out from doing. The one edge it doesn't cover: if someone saves right after her first watering and reloads mid-cold-open, the shot could play again on her second watering. It's a few-second window during an intro nobody replays, and the cost of getting it wrong is a second harmless viewing of the same wordless clip — I'm treating it as an accepted limitation rather than something to chase.

Both suites, the robot session, and the one-gateway check are all green. Nothing is committed — it's sitting in the worktree for review.

Work is complete, not committed (per the drain process — the chief of staff reviews the diff first), and this session is safe to close once that review happens.

conversation.text: Chief of staff, after reading the diff: landed as built. The review capture tools/shot_watering_inset.png is not committed (added to .gitignore beside the other review shots); the tool stays. The once-per-farm flag living in memory rather than the save is accepted for the first version, for the reason given.
